sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Angelina, a veteran courier in the service of Rhodes Island, whose footsteps have reached most of the nations known to us so far. She also serves as a veteran Caster Operator, aiding Rhodes Island with her singular Originium Arts.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 7%
Compared to her condition shortly after she first arrived at Rhodes Island, the progression of her infection has been slight, and can be said to be rather well controlled.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.24u/L
Although Angelina is careful enough in her protective measures, this figure still cannot be brought down to a level that would be entirely reassuring.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Rhodes Island has no shortage of field Operators who have made real achievements in Originium Arts, some of whom could be called masters. But ask which Operator has made the most remarkable progress during her time at Rhodes Island, and the great majority of Arts-oriented field Operators will bring up Angelina's name.
When Angelina first began taking part in field work, Rhodes Island classified her as an apprentice Caster Operator, not wishing to place too heavy a burden on her during field missions. Angelina's primary role, however, was not that of a Caster but of a courier. She rarely stayed at Rhodes Island for long, and even aboard the Landship she was usually busy collecting and packing parcels, so she could hardly find an opportunity to sit the certification test for apprentice Casters. As a result she carried the title of 'apprentice Caster Operator' for a very long time, and it was only when her schedule finally opened up that she nervously took the test—and ended up putting no small amount of mental pressure on the apprentice Operators who took the field after her.
Even after passing the test without trouble, Angelina still feels there is much about her Arts that needs improving, and she has been working toward it ever since—though she can hardly be faulted for chasing perfection. Influencing gravity is an exceedingly rare gift, and there is no one aboard Rhodes Island who can guide her hand in hand. What is more, these Originium Arts are extraordinarily difficult to control and almost impossible to land at a hundred-percent success rate, which likewise colors Angelina's assessment of her own ability.
In any case, after this trip to Rim Billiton, Angelina is plainly far more confident than she was before. No one feels this more keenly than Croissant, who is on very good terms with her. The two of them often hold 'Arts vs. Brawn' weightlifting contests. At first they only compared sheer weight, but once Angelina's control over her Arts reached a new level, they began competing over who could lift heavy and hold steady. After that, Croissant could only pull off the occasional upset with rules like 'stack a whole tower of suitcases and balance a little ball on top without letting it fall'—until this most recent match...

No matter how heavy it is, once I've lifted it she just lifts me and the whole load together! Nobody's ever going to challenge her to lifting again, boo hoo hoo...
—Croissant

That said, when Angelina used her Arts to arrange the weights into a staircase in midair and invited Croissant to climb to the top and take in the view, Croissant accepted the invitation with great enthusiasm all the same.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
Whatever the level of her Originium Arts, Angelina's foremost identity at Rhodes Island remains that of a Rhodes Island courier.
There is, in truth, not a great deal we can say on this front, for the simple reason that a competent courier leaves little for others to talk about. The parcel is delivered, the letter arrives, and the courier's figure naturally fades from sight. Yet for all that silence, a courier inevitably comes to know a great many things—who wrote to whom, who received a letter and never wrote back, whose address keeps changing... Fragments like these alone can be pieced together into truths that are not always so very vague. And so many couriers regard silence—or at least silence at the right moment—as a virtue.
Couriers born in Siracusa understand this better than most, and Angelina is no exception. She is, of course, an utterly ordinary girl, happy to talk fashion, trends, and dressing up with girls her age—but there are also many times when she hides her feelings and swallows them down, letting the things that once set her heart pounding slowly dry out and weather away into secrets she will never speak aloud.
We have no intention of meddling in how a courier goes about her work, but we do hope that Angelina can spend this one-of-a-kind stretch of her life in the way she truly wishes to. The best support we can offer her is to answer her kindness and her sense of duty with unconditional trust.
She has clearly realized as much. She is now the most senior of the couriers in long-term service at Rhodes Island—second to none in the number of parcels sent and delivered and in her completion record—and she often offers her own views on matters of logistics. At the same time, she has come more and more to see Rhodes Island as a place she can truly trust, truly lean on, and truly be herself in. She decorates her dorm to her own taste, leaves a little gift for the doctor after a physical, and when she is restless, walks wordlessly into the game room to play all day, or sits down in the cafeteria and works through carton after carton of ice cream at a measured but unbroken pace.

So you really didn't use your Arts when you got on the scale?
—Tani, curious

Who would step onto a scale still carrying an Arts Unit?!
—Angelina, not knowing whether to laugh or cry

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
What Angelina's journey to Rim Billiton brought us was, first of all, three new Operators of wildly differing temperaments; second, data on the active Originium in Rim Billiton's southern reaches; and last, some news concerning the so-called followers of Hilda.
Those people, however, stood far too far out on the fringes of her following. One of them, after leaving Red Sand Town in Uluru's company, drifted from place to place until he reached one of Rhodes Island's offices, where he spent the last of his days. By his account, even the man at the very center of their circle never dared to claim that he had laid eyes on Hilda.
On her later journeys through Rim Billiton, Angelina looked into the backgrounds of these people more than once, and managed to piece together the histories of a few of them and how they came to be led astray—but the great majority of the leads eventually went cold.

[Classified Log]
'That great Wayfarer set out from Rim Billiton, and in Rim Billiton she shall at last raise her transcendent kingdom.'
This was a rumor Angelina overheard in a poor quarter of Ultimate Big Iron Town. She was unable to trace the speaker, but the words have stayed on her mind ever since.

Setting the incident at Red Sand Town aside, Angelina is herself Infected. Her condition was very poor when she first came to Rhodes Island, and even now her Oripathy is not entirely without signs of worsening. What is more, one of the friends she made on this trip, Jacinta, is a patient in the middle-to-late stages of Oripathy... We were genuinely worried that all of these factors together might take a toll on Angelina's state of mind.
Unexpectedly, this was how Angelina answered us:
'I'm not going to say things like "there's always a way." Some things simply have no way out. All we can do is watch them happen, delay them as much as we can and mend what we can—and even at our very best, more often than not we don't get the ending we wanted.
'But no matter what, I won't lose hope. The hope the Doctor first gave me... did have something unrealistic in it, yet even a false hope was precious to me. I'd even say that without that little bit of hope, there's no way I would still be standing in front of everyone like this today.
'And besides, even if that hope wasn't built on entirely solid ground, the feeling behind it was never false.'

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
...And so another jar was filled to the brim with paper stars.
The truth is, before long even I couldn't tell what I was folding these stars for anymore. It had become a habit—when I'd sent a letter off, when I'd managed to do something, when I'd failed to do something, when I'd said something I felt a little proud of thinking back on it, when there was something I couldn't bring myself to say...
But if all I do is fold paper, if I just hide how I feel inside a paper star... then some things will never be known to anyone else. Stars don't speak. Stars are silent eyes. They know, but they never tell. No one knows what a star is thinking.
And me... I know I can't go on shining in the sky forever the way the stars do. Martina says that feelings kept hidden in your heart will change one day, but for me, maybe at some moment before those feelings have changed at all, I'll already have become that meteor streaking across the horizon. So I ought to be brave and say it out loud—to say how much I miss Mom and Dad, how attached I am to Rhodes Island, how much I care about my friends—and to say the words buried deepest in my heart... to say them to the people who matter to me, so that I leave behind no more regrets.
Mm, that's all the paper stars Angelina has. And if there's still something too embarrassing to say out loud just yet... then use this—the paper-folded Vulpo Beast Steward my mother first taught me to make, the 'little fox.'
It isn't a star, so it doesn't have to spend the rest of its life waiting for a companion star. It goes and finds the person it wants to be with, stays by their side, leans on them—and now and then, lets itself be leaned on.
Not just for embraces and dances, but as the one you can put your back against in danger, the shoulder that holds you up when your strength runs out.

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
[Audio Log]
It's all right. I just finished training, so the timing's perfect—it's not early at all.
Uh... no. It's nothing urgent that I came to see you about. Is that not okay? If you have something more important to attend to—
Mm—okay, all right! I'm really happy that the Doctor would set aside time just for me.
So here's the thing. A while ago I delivered a letter that meant a great deal to Miss Gitano, and in return she read my fortune... a very serious reading, one that took a lot out of her.
She saw me in her crystal ball—she said it must be me in the future... But that isn't really the important part. What matters is that I was in the middle of a war, and it looked as though I was holding a defensive line.
No matter how many field missions I take on for Rhodes Island, I'm still a courier. If a war ever reaches the point where even couriers are duty-bound to fight, then what... what would have become of Rhodes Island, or even of this whole land?
...It would be a lie to say I'm not afraid. That future frightens me. Even though Miss Gitano later saw some different scenes as well, that hazy battlefield still shows up in my dreams. That's why I came to you.
The me in the crystal ball? Um... Miss Gitano said that figure of mine showed no fear at all... If the me of that time really can manage it, then I'd be so glad.
But... if we really do have to face a war, I hope I can still get excited over a meal made with care, feel relieved by a letter saying someone is safe, let my brow relax a little at a carefully blended scent... and keep at least a moment to spare for a flower that has just come into bloom.
You don't know whether you can make that wish come true, but you'll work toward it anyway?
That makes me really happy. But I might... have one more request that's a little much to ask.
Could this... become your wish as well?
...Thank you, Doctor.
Just like you, I'll give this wish... everything I have.
